Lena (CS): AcmeHealth reached out asking for a quota bump for embeddings — pilot goes live Mon. Current usage ~10k req/day, they want to run ~50k/day during the pilot and expect some short bursts. Can we triage for fraud/abuse before we increase? Ticket #3887
Mike (Support): Got it. Support ticket https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-3887. Customer asked for up to 60 RPS bursts but average ~0.6 RPS. Billing on file. Sample keys: key_7f3a... They reported a burst last night ~21:40 UTC.
Tara (Sales): Timeline? customer asks if we can approve before their demo Tues. Is a short-term dev bump possible? :eyes:
Priya (FraudOps): I can do a quick review. Need recent request patterns (per-key), account age, payment method, geo distribution, and any anomalous user-agent or token reuse. Also check for high similarity across embedding outputs (indicates scraping).
Diego (SRE): Our default per-account soft cap is 100 RPS with a hard cap at 300 RPS. For Hosteds we can apply a temporary override but want Fraud sign-off. I recommend a staged increase: 1) provisional override -> 60 RPS and 50k/day for 48h, 2) enable tracing and alerts for error rate and token rate, 3) rollback if we see abuse signals. Example admin command:
```
redwood admin quotas set acme-health --rps 60 --daily 50000 --policy temp-48h
```
Will also enable the per-key sampling hooks.
Anna (PM): If we're going to enable temporary overrides frequently we should capture this flow as an internal runbook and add a small UI affordance for provisional increases. For this request: what's the launch criteria? (fraud green, <1% 5xx, <5% anomalous UA). Add to backlog if we need permanent product work.
Lena (CS): Decision from this thread: propose APPROVE conditional increase to 60 RPS / 50k/day for 48h, require IP allowlist or SSO to reduce account takeover risk, require customer contact person and expected traffic windows. Rollback triggers: sustained >10% 5xx or sustained >90% capacity for 2h with no response. Priya, please confirm you can do the checks before I enact.
Priya (FraudOps): I'll run quick checks now. Please attach raw logs for 24h around the burst. I'll look for token reuse, identical payload patterns, rapid key rotation, and odd geos. If everything looks normal I'll mark as approved.
Mike (Support): Pasted small log snippet from last night (redacted):
```
2026-02-21T21:39:58Z key=key_7f3a client_ip=18.205.1.9 endpoint=/v1/embeddings size=512 status=200
2026-02-21T21:40:01Z key=key_7f3a client_ip=18.205.1.9 endpoint=/v1/embeddings size=512 status=200
2026-02-21T21:40:02Z key=key_7f3a client_ip=18.205.1.9 endpoint=/v1/embeddings size=512 status=200
2026-02-21T21:41:20Z key=key_1a8b client_ip=54.230.11.2 endpoint=/v1/embeddings size=512 status=429
```
Mike (Support): Also attached ticket notes about payment method and contact.
Priya (FraudOps): Quick findings: account created 2025-11-03, billing on card ending 4242, geo mostly us-east, user-agent looks like `python-requests/2.31.0` with a small cluster of requests from 18.205.1.9. No evidence of token stuffing or rapid key churn. I want to enable higher-sample tracing for 2h once override is live. If we see identical embeddings repeated across different inputs that's a red flag.
Diego (SRE): OK. I'll stage the override and enable the tracing hooks and an alert that pings #incidents + @Priya if 5xx > 1% over 5m or error count increases 3x baseline.
Lena (CS): Thanks. I'll tell the customer: conditional 48h increase approved pending monitoring. Customer must provide IP ranges or SSO, and will be rate-limited back if abuse signals appear.
Tara (Sales): Great — will tell them demo is green but emphasize conditional nature. :thumbsup:
Anna (PM): I'll create a small backlog ticket to formalize provisional overrides and add telemetry fields for easier fraud sign-off (owner, attestations, rollback criteria).
Priya (FraudOps): Marking as approved to proceed with staged override. I'll keep monitoring and post updates in this thread.
Mike (Support): Done. Updated ticket RED-3887 with approval notes and assigned follow-up tasks.
Lena (CS): Closing loop here; will reopen if anything pops up. Thanks everyone. :tada:
